change_refusals.meaning: the record changed after the writer read it; carries the current version
another request changed the record; carries the case id and the brief reference

host_roles.gateway: talks to people through channels and the web
host_roles.installation_authority: issues and revokes certificates and authority keys
host_roles.team_services: the team's operations, steering, access and custody services

access.decision.description: What became of an access request, sent to the waiting task.

access.request.description: A task asks the team services for access; no model decides it.

access.resolved.description: A person's decision on an access request, from the gateway to the team services.

access.review.description: An access review for the gateway's Inbox, from the team services; a refused decision returns this way too.

access.withdraw.description: The lead withdraws a task's access request.

agent.exit.description: Stop an agent after its current step.

agent.pause.description: Pause one agent at its next safe point; it keeps its queued work.

agent.status.description: An agent's status: basic for anyone allowed, full only for the team's lead.

conflicts.cancel.description: An administrator cancels a change conflict.

conflicts.decide.description: A person decides a change conflict.

conflicts.list.description: Open and recent change conflicts, for administrators.

credential.form.request.description: Ask the gateway to collect, set up or delete a credential through a secure form.

credential.form.result.description: What became of a credential form.

custody.decide.description: The lead reassigns a task or adopts late work.

custody.moved.description: Tells a former holder that its task moved; later results are kept as late work.

debug.dump.description: Turn an agent's diagnostic context dumps on or off.

delivery.receipt.description: The gateway delivered an answer or notice to a person.

delivery.refused.description: A receiver refused a message; sent back to its sender.

dlq.notice.description: A receiver set a message aside; the exact bytes are at dlq.raw.<copy>, and the notice holds identifiers only.

heartbeat_items.add.description: The lead adds a heartbeat item.

heartbeat_items.disable.description: The lead disables a heartbeat item.

heartbeat_items.enable.description: The lead enables a heartbeat item.

heartbeat_items.list.description: The lead reads heartbeat items and their versions.

heartbeat_items.remove.description: The lead removes a heartbeat item.

heartbeat_items.update.description: The lead changes a heartbeat item.

host.join.description: A new host asks to join the installation; the frame is signed with the key it presents.

host.renew.description: A host renews its certificate and connection credential, or rotates its keys.

intent.set.description: The lead states a request's current intent.

knowledge.add_note.description: Add a note to a knowledge page.

knowledge.count_contributions.description: How many contributions wait for a curator.

knowledge.merge.description: A curator merges a page into another.

knowledge.publish_contribution.description: Publish a contribution, edited or as it is.

knowledge.resolve_note.description: A curator resolves a note on a page.

knowledge.revert.description: Revert a knowledge page to an earlier revision.

knowledge.write.description: Create or edit a knowledge page.

ledger.fact.description: A fact for an agent's work ledger from the team services.

memory.replace.description: Change only the supplied fields of a memory fact.

objectives.abandon.description: Abandon one of the person's Objectives.

objectives.activate_plan.description: Start runtime-owned execution of the active task's semantic plan steps.

objectives.delete.description: Delete one of the person's Objectives.

objectives.get.description: The lead reads an Objective's full record and agent-update version.

objectives.pause.description: Pause one of the person's Objectives.

objectives.record_checkpoint.description: Save a continuation checkpoint for the active Objective work session.

objectives.resume.description: Resume one of the person's Objectives.

objectives.start_task.description: Queue a continuation task for an Objective and its current plan.

objectives.stop.description: Stop one of the person's Objectives.

objectives.update_progress.description: The lead records progress on an Objective.

objectives.update_status.description: The lead changes an Objective's status.

objectives.work_profiles.apply.description: Apply the exact Objective work-profile proposal the person accepted.

objectives.work_profiles.list.description: Read configured profiles, the person's installed profiles and latest proposals.

objectives.work_profiles.propose.description: Persist an inert exact Objective work-profile proposal for the person.

objectives.work_profiles.remove.description: Remove the person's reusable profile after explicit confirmation.

objectives.work_sessions.disable.description: Disable bounded work sessions after the person agrees.

objectives.work_sessions.enable.description: Enable explicitly accepted bounded work sessions on an Objective.

objectives.work_sessions.start.description: Open a requested work session on the active Objective-linked task.

objectives.work_sessions.status.description: Read an owned Objective's policy, recent sessions, checkpoints and tuning observations.

people.set_standing.description: Settle a person's work after their standing changed.

person.notify.description: A notice for a person, delivered by the gateway.

question.closed.description: A question ended without an answer.

requests.pause.description: The lead pauses its own request's work.

requests.resume.description: The lead resumes its own request's work.

run_context.sign.description: A worker running a scheduled job asks the scheduler for the run's authority token.

schedules.authorize_access.description: Hand on access for a saved schedule policy and end obsolete setup grants.

schedules.get.description: Read complete safe details of one visible schedule, in JSON text pages.

schedules.inspect_worker.description: Inspect worker assignment and startup diagnostics for a schedule.

schedules.install.description: Install a schedule: create, replace, ensure or refresh it.

schedules.list.description: The schedules the caller may see.

schedules.pause.description: Pause a schedule until a time.

schedules.prepare_access.description: Preview worker readiness and missing access without starting the job.

schedules.set_worker.description: Save a schedule's worker type, startup policy and capability requirements.

schedules.update.description: Change a schedule's name, instruction, timing, controls or run notes.

skills.changed.description: Hint that a managed skill was installed or removed. Receivers verify the stored receipt before they refresh.

staged_changes.apply.description: The lead applies a staged change the person reviewed.

steering.decide.description: The lead decides what each held task changes, or extends the hold once.

task.account.description: A held holder's account of where its task stopped.

task.handback.description: A holder that lost its lease returns a task.

task.probe.description: Whether the holder still has a task, asked by the watchdog.

task.progress.description: Where a task stands, from its holder to its requester.

task.question.description: A question from a task's holder to the one who can answer it.

task.report.description: A report from a holder to its requester; the lead decides whether a person sees it.

task.request.description: Give a task to an agent or a pool.

task.result.description: The final answer of a task, sent by its holder.

task.steer.description: Steering for the holder of one named task.

task.stop.description: Stop one task. Sent only to the task's current holder.

tasks.cancel.description: Stop a task, a conversation's work, a delivery's work or all of the person's work.

tasks.inventory.description: The person's running work and schedules.

tasks.probe.description: Whether a task the person owns is still known.

tasks.progress.description: Where the person's request in one conversation stands.

tasks.purge.description: Remove every queued task that is not running from an agent's queue.

tasks.remove.description: Remove one queued task from an agent's queue.

tasks.steer.description: The person's guidance for a running request; stored before it is accepted.

tool.setup.request.description: Ask the gateway to have a person or administrator set a tool up.

tool.setup.result.description: What became of a tool setup.

agent.description: An agent's state, written by the host it is placed on when the state changes.
agent.write_rule: written on change, at most once per 2 seconds; readers accept it only from the placement's host

agent_session.description: An agent session certificate, issued by the team services that place the agent.
agent_session.write_rule: rewritten with a higher sequence to renew it or to record its actual end; kept until its end plus the longest kind lifetime

agreement.description: A federation agreement with another installation.
agreement.write_rule: rewritten with a higher sequence to change or end it; only the receiver's own authority signs it

certificate.write_rule: written once; kept until its expiry plus the longest kind lifetime, so queued frames can still be checked

host.description: A runtime host's liveness and capacity, written by the host itself every 20 seconds.
host.write_rule: written by the host itself every 20 seconds; a host writes only its own record

placement.description: Which host runs an agent; its key-value revision is the fencing token.
placement.write_rule: compare-and-set on the last revision; the revision is the fencing token

revocations.write_rule: rewritten with a higher sequence on each revocation; the revocation epoch only grows and entries are never removed while a revoked certificate could still be named

team_view.description: One entry of a team's shared view of its members, requests, tasks and Objectives.
team_view.write_rule: deleted when the item closes; each entry at most 4 KiB

verification_refusals.meaning: the serialized frame is larger than max_frame_bytes
the frame is not one JSON object, repeats a key, holds a number with a fraction or exponent part, or breaks the frame schema

the trust store holds no certificate for the issuer's installation, runtime and membership epoch that names the issuer's key id and was valid when the frame was issued, or the installation is neither the receiver's nor one it has an agreement with; a join (verification proof_of_possession) must instead name the key it presents in its body, and a key id the trust store already knows must keep its public key
the signature is not the one unpadded base64url spelling of a signature that verifies over the canonical frame with the certificate's key
the body digest does not match the body
the issuer's certificate, or the certificate that signed the issuer's agent session, is listed in its installation's revocations, whenever it was revoked and whenever the frame says it was issued

the issuer's certificate has a membership or revocation epoch below the receiver's minimum for that runtime or installation (request/reply and events only; queued work is judged by the certificate valid when it was issued, and a join by the key it presents)

the issuer's revocation epoch or team disagrees with its certificate; or it names an agent without a session, or a session that does not place that agent, of a type the certificate allows, on the signing runtime when the frame was issued; or a reply does not come from the agent and team the request was for

none of the certificate's roles may send the kind to its audience's address (for a reply, receive its request); or the frame comes from another installation with a kind, class or destination team its agreement does not allow; or it crosses the outside boundary other than through the lead (an outside agent's adapter reaches only the lead's inbox, and only a lead agent or the team services reach an outside agent)
the frame is for another installation or team

the subject is not ua.v1.<audience team>.<sender slot>.<address> for the kind and audience target, the frame arrived on another subject, or a NATS header copy disagrees with the frame; replies use the audience runtime's inbox and name their request
the receiver's clock, less the clock tolerance, is at or after the frame's expiry or its kind's lifetime
the frame's issue or not-before time is more than the clock tolerance ahead of the receiver's clock
a frame with the same issuer installation, runtime, membership epoch and message id was admitted with other content
the kind is not in this registry
the body breaks the kind's schema or body rules, or the idempotency key is not the one the kind's key parts give

the frame carries an authority token its kind does not take or lacks one it requires; or the token is not signed by a gateway or scheduler certificate of its own installation, names a schedule without a scheduler's signature, names another team than the issuer's, was not valid when the frame was issued, names neither a person nor a schedule (system work), lasts longer than authority_token_max_seconds (command_token_max_seconds when bound to a command), is bound to a type of record its kind does not take, is of a type the sender's roles may not present on that address, or is bound to another record than the body field its kind's binding names (at) or, for a binding without one, than the task the handler holds; or a change-conflict decision token in the body is not signed by a team-services certificate of the frame's installation and team, or was not valid when the frame was issued
the receiver's access decision refused the sender
